card.statement: Check whether the installed learned router actually executes the FP32-weight GEMM targeted by the proposed Hopper BF16x3 kernel. The supplied constructor requests FP32 output, which establishes neither weight dtype nor active GEMM execution; hash routing may further reduce eligible work. A three-hour loader and dispatch audit is therefore the first decision point. If an eligible baseline branch is active and an equivalent optimization is absent, qualify a minimal kernel port while retaining Marlin experts and communication. Count actual padded token rows, not requests. Author-reported H200 results justify inspecting this hardware-specific lead, but different model shapes and cache conditions leave DeepSeek savings unknown. Complete kernel source and numerical qualification remain prerequisites.
card.observed_bottleneck: No local router bottleneck is observed. Nominal source shows GateLinear construction and hash-routing state. Author-reported PR61903 results concern H200 kernels and other-model workloads; no matched DeepSeek-V4.1 service result is supplied. Installed weights, active dispatch, affected layers, source membership and timing share are unknown.
card.mechanism: Affected-event frequency: learned-router calls meeting actual weight/activation dtype, shape, padded-row and dispatch predicates; exclude bypasses and unaffected small-row calls. Component occupied time: eligible GEMM plus casts and dispatch overhead. Exposed time: its contribution to the target or draft dependency chain, without summing ranks as wall time. Expected net saving: measured exposed per-call reduction weighted by native calls, minus conversion, warmup and resource-contention costs. Service transfer: routing arithmetic can alter subsequent expert work, so local kernel speed and quality must be checked before the frozen service test.
card.proposed_change: Inspect installed loader/forward hashes, checkpoint-to-parameter dtype transformations, learned/hash routing branches, actual shapes, batch-invariant controls and any existing SM90 optimization. Stop if the path is ineligible or already optimized. If eligibility passes, require the exact proposed kernel revision and complete warmup/dispatch implementation before a minimal port. Preserve expert backend, routing policy, activation formats outside the router, allgather_reducescatter and graph configuration. Apply cutoffs only where the exact proposed dispatch supports them.
card.code_surface: Actual installed counterparts of vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py, V4.1 inheritance and GateLinear loading/forward/JIT dispatch. The supplied constructor is nominal upstream source, not installed attestation. PR61903 names sm90_bf16x3_router_gemm and VllmJitKernel warmup, but supplies no kernel implementation or exact inspected kernel revision.
card.applicability: Three-hour eligibility audit ready. Implementation and GPU qualification remain held pending actual dtype/branch evidence and complete source. H200 matches the proposal's architecture, but DeepSeek shape and numerical compatibility are unknown. The reported 24-token cutoff applies to specified GEMV shapes, not automatically every local router. Full experiment not ready.
card.predicted_direction: Primary metric: frozen Mooncake 0.5x median long-output ITL. Numerical low/base/high optimization deltas are unknown. Ineligible or already optimized routing supplies zero baseline delta; rare or unexposed calls can make a faster kernel immaterial. Benefit requires repeated eligible expensive calls with preserved downstream behavior. Measure actual dtypes, branch frequency, padded shapes, graph-contained and exposed timing, and routing changes before estimating any service improvement. Other-model H200 gains are not transferred.

experiment.control: Actual installed GateLinear dispatch on identical loaded weights and recorded activations, including its existing small-row GEMV wherever legal. Do not force SGEMM when a faster installed path is already selected. Compare complete router calls, including casts and dispatch.
experiment.treatment: Cheapest pilot: three engineering hours of CPU/source/metadata eligibility work, zero GPU-hours. Establish an active eligible baseline branch and absence of an equivalent optimization. If these cannot be established, defer. After exact kernel review, allow one 30-minute standalone SM90 shape/correctness allocation, then only on success two 60-minute all-rank integration allocations. Total wall cap 150 minutes on eight allocated GPUs=20 GPU-hours; no retries. Freeze shapes, fixtures, phase windows and analysis before timing.
experiment.metrics: Weight/activation dtypes, installed hashes, target/draft role, learned/hash branch, real/padded rows and eligible call counts. Measure complete graph-contained router duration, exposed dependency time, conversion/dispatch cost, numerical errors, ordered top-k identities and routing weights. Require twenty eligible calls per affected role/rank in each fixed window, complete layer attribution and valid timing. Later retain frozen ITL, separate request TPOT, exact tokens, TTFT/E2E tails, all-rank speculation counters, KV/preemption, replay lag, goodput and quality.
experiment.supports_if: The baseline branch is active and eligible, equivalent optimization is absent, exact local shapes compile, and conservative numerical/graph gates pass. Use twelve fixed paired replay blocks with alternating order and a 95% block-resampled interval, treating them as technical component units. Require positive lower-bound exposed savings against the fastest legal installed path and a conservative native-frequency opportunity proxy reaching 2%. Kernel speed alone does not qualify a service attempt. Any full evaluation retains the positive screen, both 3% tail guards, five alternating matched full-run confirmation pairs for small gains and the existing 2% promotion criterion.
experiment.rejects_if: Stop for ineligible weights, bypassed GEMM, an already active equivalent optimization, unsupported local shapes, numerical/quality failure or scope-expanding precision changes. With adequate timing, stop allocation for unfavorable net savings or an upper-bound opportunity proxy below 2%. Do not change workload or router precision merely to create eligibility.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Loaded dtype/dispatch cannot be established, exact proposed source is unavailable, branch telemetry or opportunity coverage is missing, numerical reference requirements are unresolved, timing attribution fails, or startup/JIT exhausts a cap. An interval crossing the materiality threshold also defers advancement. Missing hits without coverage are not proof of zero opportunity.
experiment.held_out_condition: Hold out graph-boundary rows, ragged DP batches, near-tied routing fixtures, long-context and mixed-prefill agent traffic, and cold/warm cache states. Preserve agent-f75 8K/1K and full fixed Mooncake anchors at seq64; isolate 1K/1K diagnostics.
experiment.correctness: Prospective conservative pilot rules: identical ordered logical top-k selections on fixed same-input real-activation fixtures; reference tie behavior; finite normalized routing weights; per-fixture mean and maximum absolute error against FP64 no worse than the installed comparator. These rules may reject an otherwise acceptable approximation and must not be relaxed after observing results. Check full-layer outputs under existing backend numerical limits, partial tiles, strided inputs, hash bypass, all warmup keys, eager/graph parity and repeated replay. Preserve relevant G01-G05 and Q02/Q04 checks, EOS/cancellation/recovery and changed-math quality qualification. Existing backend and quality thresholds are not supplied, so their prospective specification remains a GPU-release prerequisite.
experiment.cost: Prospective estimates; actual implementation effort is unknown and no work is executed here. Inspection: estimated 1-3 engineering hours, cap 3; GPU 0. Implementation/correctness: provisional 8-20 engineering hours, cap 20 including—not adding—a four-hour feasibility checkpoint. GPU compilation/correctness cap is 4 GPU-hours in the 30-minute standalone slot, included in the total pilot. Instrumentation/pilot analysis: 4-8 engineering hours, cap 8; two integration slots add 16 GPU-hours. Total qualification ceiling 20 GPU-hours includes startup, JIT, capture, tests, warmup, measurement, export and cleanup. Historical model startup was about 26 minutes per arm; shape compilation and fixtures remain unknown. Separate conditional screen: 3-6 engineering hours, cap 6, 20 GPU-hours. Confirmation: 6-12 engineering hours, cap 12, 100 GPU-hours for five full pairs. Held-out allowance: 2-4 engineering hours, cap 4, 20 GPU-hours. Service arms have 75-minute eight-GPU caps; no retries. Monetary cost=P times allocated GPU-hours/8; node price and cost-per-token savings are unknown.

card.revision_reason: Repairs prior H03's ambiguous support condition: eligibility now requires an active qualifying baseline branch and absence of equivalent optimization. The feasibility checkpoint is explicitly included within the implementation cap, and local numerical, timing and uncertainty gates are specified. Missing installed and proposed kernel evidence remains pending. Existing family C01 keeps its externally reported grouped hold and distinct untested indexed arm; this router intervention does not reopen either. C19's expert-backend work is unchanged.

baseline_relative_value.rationale: Replacing an active, exposed router SGEMM has a credible path to lower cycle time. The proposal correctly treats "out_dtype=torch.float32," as insufficient evidence of FP32 weights or execution and supplies a three-hour eligibility check. This satisfies the rubric's inspection alternative. Local branch eligibility, affected layers, padded-row distribution and net savings remain unknown, making this the least established baseline delta.

bounded_pilot_decision.rationale: The pilot checks actual dispatch, fastest legal baseline paths, exact shapes, graph replay, numerical behavior and native opportunity coverage before service allocation. Its conservative routing-parity gate is legitimate and prospectively stated. Missing dtype evidence, kernel source, numerical thresholds or timing attribution defer advancement. The native-frequency proxy and complete quality criteria still require specification before GPU execution.

engineering_time_and_fit.rationale: Caps are 3 hours inspection, 20 implementation/correctness including the four-hour checkpoint, and 8 instrumentation/analysis. H200 matches the proposed SM90 architecture, and expert computation and transport remain fixed. Nevertheless, the supplied constructor is nominal upstream code; actual loader/forward behavior and the complete proposed kernel are absent. Local dispatch, warmup and numerical fit cannot yet be established.

evaluation_gpu_budget.rationale: One 30-minute standalone allocation plus two 60-minute integration allocations correctly totals 150 minutes and 20 GPU-hours across eight allocated GPUs. The CPU eligibility audit comes first; startup/JIT/correctness and cleanup are included, and cap exhaustion is inconclusive. Later 20/100/20 GPU-hour service stages are separate. Node price and cost-per-token improvement remain unknown.

evidence_and_history.rationale: Static evidence establishes GateLinear construction and hash-routing state, not active eligible weights. PR61903 author reports concern H200 kernels and other-model workloads, including cold-L2 measurements; these are not matched DeepSeek results. Its qualification "on the fp32 GEMV shapes" limits the 24-token cutoff. The proposal preserves those distinctions and does not reopen grouped C01 or claim an expert-backend result.

objections: FP32 output, checkpoint metadata and an inherited constructor do not independently establish loaded FP32 weights or a qualifying executed branch. Eligibility requires the installed loader/forward chain and, before advancement, runtime witnesses.
The exact proposed kernel revision and full warmup/dispatch implementation are missing. Architecture matching alone cannot establish legal DeepSeek shapes or graph compatibility.
Cold-L2 speedups and unrelated-model TPOT improvements cannot establish native router materiality. Preserve unaffected GEMV/hash paths in the denominator and measure complete calls, including casts.

Exact ordered top-k parity and per-fixture error dominance may conservatively reject a usable approximation. That is acceptable, but full-layer tolerances and changed-math quality thresholds must be fixed before observing results.

Before porting, establish actual loaded dtypes, active branches, installed optimization membership and exact local shapes. Before GPU release, pin complete kernel/warmup source, numerical and quality thresholds, coverage strata and the materiality calculation.
